verdict.reasoning: Patient reports “terrible headaches since midday on the left side… I just feel like I need to vomit” and later confirms vomiting twice (“Yeah, I vomited twice.”). Headache is described as throbbing (“Yeah, I guess it's throbbing on that left side.”).
Patient states: “I noticed some zigzag lines in my vision.”
Doctor asks if vision changes were in both eyes or just left; patient replies: “It feels like it's on both.” and previously said vision blurred before headache.
Doctor asks about bright lights; patient answers: “Yeah, well, I'm wearing, wearing sunglasses right now. You know, light's really hurting my eyes.” indicating photophobia requiring sunglasses.
Patient says: “like if I lean forward or like move my head or neck. Yeah, the headache gets worse.” This indicates worsening with head and neck movement.
Patient explicitly states: “if I lean forward… the headache gets worse.”

Patient: “I did have a similar headache a few weeks ago.” When asked, “How long did it last?” patient responds: “For a couple of days.” and “Yeah, I had to take painkillers and had to go to bed and rest and had a couple days off work.”

Patient denies fever (“No, I don't feel feverish.”), rash (“No, I haven't noticed anything like that.”), speech problems (“No.”), limb numbness/weakness (“No.”), balance issues (“No.”), and head injury (“No.” to recent fall or being knocked on the head).
When asked about medical history, patient says: “No.” No other past conditions are mentioned.
Patient states: “I take the pill, microgynon.” and clarifies duration and indication: “Three months.” and “It's for contraception.”
Patient: “My mum had. Has migraines, but I've not been diagnosed.”
Patient adds: “My mum has an underactive thyroid as well.” which corresponds to hypothyroidism.
Doctor asks about family history of brain cancer: “Any other family history of that?” Patient replies: “No.”
Doctor asks: “Who's at home with you?” Patient replies: “I live on my own.”

Patient: “working fashion industry and you know, they're wondering what's going on… managers like putting a lot of pressure on me to deliver… it's not a good time.” indicating a stressful fashion industry job.
Doctor asks: “Do you smoke at all?” Patient: “No.” Then: “And do you drink much in the way of alcohol?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “Do you do much in the way of exercise?” Patient: “No.” indicating minimal exercise.
Doctor: “what kind of things do you do to alleviate your stress? Normally?” Patient: “Nothing really.” indicating no coping strategies.
Transcript only mentions a plan to examine (“Normally at this I'd like to kind of proceed to examination”) but no vital signs or physical exam findings are actually documented.

Doctor states: “I wonder whether you may. May have a migraine. Migraine type headache. It sounds very classical of that nature. The headache on one side, throbbing nature, the nausea, vomiting, sensitive to bright lights.” and patient had visual zigzag lines (aura).

Doctor: “I'm reassured that you don't have anything more serious, such as meningitis or indeed brain cancer.” This reassurance is based on absence of focal neurologic symptoms and fever/rash (“No” answers to speech problems, limb issues, balance issues, fever, rash). While not phrased as ‘rule out’, the assessment uses these negatives to exclude serious intracranial pathology.
Doctor: “Some strong painkillers would be advisable. So, you know, think about paracetamol or even cocodamol and some anti inflammatories such as ibuprofen and naproxen.”
Doctor: “I think keeping a headache diary will be quite important to see exactly what's triggering these headaches.”

Doctor: “if your headaches were to become more persistent, then we can maybe think about giving you some medications that will stop your headaches from happening in the first place. Something prophylactic medicines.”
Doctor: “we can have a discussion next time I see you next week, perhaps.” indicating reevaluation next week.

Doctor: “if your symptoms aren't getting better in the next two, three days, or indeed they're getting worse, I'd like you to come back… if your headache's getting worse and not responding to medications, or your neck pain is getting worse, or you develop any weakness in your arms and legs or your vision, then I want you to come back and see me straight away.”
